{panel:bgColor=#e3fcef}
*OVERALL QA STATUS: PASSED*
{panel}

Tested today on the QA branch [https://sv9658.qa.shopview.com] (build {{v26.39.1-2e57b93}}), with production {{app.shopview.com}} (build {{v26.39.2-1aeb22d}}) used to capture the before-state. All 9 checks passed.

In plain terms: on the build our customers are running today, once you pick an existing part on a purchase order line you can still type a different product's name over its description — which is how two products end up merged into one in inventory. On this branch that field belongs to the part and cannot be retyped, and when the part you want genuinely does not exist yet there is now an option to create it, even while the search is showing matches.

h3. Before and after — the description

!01-description-lock.png|width=900,height=882!

_Production on the left of the pair, the fix branch below it. On production part {{1237944}} is "A158", and its description was freely retyped to "Hitch Lunette Ring 3 Inch". On the branch the field is greyed out, holds the part's own name, and clicking it and typing changes nothing._

h3. Before and after — somewhere to go

!02-create-new-part.png|width=900,height=1144!

_This is why people reached for the description box: it was the only field that moved. On production a partial part number listed 24 matches and offered no way to create a new part — I scrolled that list to its end to be sure. On the branch "Add new special order part" sits under the matches._

h3. The customer's own case

!03-customer-case.png|width=900,height=488!

_Part number {{BUYPH20}} belongs to "20 TON PINTLE HOOK" — the exact pair of products from the ticket. Typing "Hitch Lunette Ring 3 Inch" over that description now does nothing, so the second product can no longer be filed under the first one's number._

h3. What I checked

||#||Check||Result||
|1|The reported problem still happens on production|*PASSED* — description retyped on an existing part, and no way to create a new one|
|2|New Purchase Order: description locks to the part and cannot be retyped|*PASSED*|
|3|The locked description survives Add, Save & Close and reopening the order|*PASSED* — order {{I9658-1395}} still shows "SV9658 product A"|
|4|Typing a different part number over it unlocks the description again|*PASSED* — becomes editable and empty, and the new part saves|
|5|"Add new special order part" appears even when the search finds matches|*PASSED* — seen with 1 match and with 11|
|6|The same three checks on an existing purchase order|*PASSED*|
|7|Editing an item already on a purchase order still allows the description to be edited|*PASSED*|
|8|Work Order → Add Part: no create option while matches are listed|*PASSED*|
|9|Parts → Returns → Create Return: a search with no matches says "No results"|*PASSED*|

h3. Two notes on the test steps

* The example in the test plan for check 5 is {{SV9658-PART-A2}}, described as still listing PART-A. It does not — the search matches on the text you type being contained in the part, so a longer string finds nothing, and that example actually exercises the empty-search case. The behaviour itself is correct and I proved it with {{SV9658}}, {{SV9658-PART}} and {{Pintle}}, all of which list matches and offer the create option.
* On Work Order → Add Part, a search with no matches shows "No results" rather than "Create ... as a new part". *Production does exactly the same*, so nothing has regressed there — it is only the test plan's wording for that line that does not match either build. That screen is not a dead end either: with Source set to Vendor the part number and description are typed straight in.

h3. What I could not check

* I did not receive a purchase order into inventory and re-confirm afterwards that the two products stay separate. The change removes the mechanism at the point of entry, and that is what I tested.
* Stock that is already merged in customers' inventories, and {{BUY-PH20}} matching {{BUYPH20}} as the same number, are out of scope for this ticket.
